title: Volume of Rectangular Prisms
objective: I can find the volume of a rectangular prism, including ones with fractional edge lengths, using base area × height.
model: rectangular prism with fractional edges, volume as base area × height, half-unit cubes filling it

widgets.component: prerequisite warm-up: 3/4 × 8, 2.5 × 4, 15 cubes per layer × 4 layers, 1 1/2 as 3/2
widgets.root: Recomputed 6, 10, 60, 3/2. These are the fraction skills the lesson needs and the right prerequisite for fractional edges.

widgets.where: Practice §2 items 1-5 (mc ×3, tbl, err), §3 items 1, 2, 5 (tbl, mc, mc) and §5 item 4 (mc)
widgets.component: support, grade-level and exit-ticket items: 4 × 3 × 5, missing height 36 ÷ 18, volume vs area, whole-number tables, box A vs B, cube 5 cm, 7 × 2 × 3
widgets.root: Every edge in these items is a whole number: they are the same kind of whole-number items as lesson 5-5's practice. The objective of 5-10 is volume with fractional edges, and the support tier, the grade-level tier and the exit check never ask for it; only 3.3, 3.4 and the warm-up touch a fraction.
widgets.replacement: Rewrite these eight items with at least one fractional or mixed-number edge, keeping the key skill: 2.1 'l = 1 1/2 in, w = 2 in, h = 4 in' (key 12 in³; distractors 7 1/2 in³ added, 8 in³ rounded 1 1/2 down to 1, 12 in² unit); 2.2 'base area 12 in², height 1/2 in' (6 in³); 2.4 table rows (2, 1 1/2, 3 → 9), (4, 2 1/2, 2 → 20), (3, 3, 1/2 → 4 1/2); 2.5 error 'dropped the 1/2'; 3.1 table with a missing fractional edge (volume 18, l = 4, w = 3 → h = 1 1/2); 3.2 'Box A 2 1/2 × 4 × 6 vs Box B 3 × 5 × 4' (60 vs 60, equal); 3.5 'cube with edges of 1 1/2 in' (3 3/8 in³); 5.4 'l = 3 1/2 ft, w = 2 ft, h = 4 ft' (28 ft³; distractors 9 1/2, 24, 28 ft²). Keep the Spanish fields and the hint ladders in step.

widgets.component: error that drops a 1/2 in height, volume of 1/2 m × 3 m × 4 m
widgets.root: Recomputed 12 in³ and 6 m³; the error is the lesson's central misconception (a fractional edge still counts).

widgets.where: Practice §4 items 1-6 and Challenge §1 items 1-6 (gen:volumePrism L1-L4)
widgets.component: generated volume problems with a drawn prism, identical to lesson 5-5's generator and levels
widgets.root: The generator was not told this is the fractional-edge lesson: assets/studio-gen/geometry.js §5 volumePrism gives a fractional edge in 0% of L1, 44% of L2 and 74% of L3 draws (L4 26%), so across the twelve slots only about 44% of items contain the lesson's idea, and the L1 items are 5-5's 'cubes of 1 ft fill the box' counts. The figure prints 7.5 while the stem says 7 1/2.
widgets.replacement: Add the item parameter p:{"frac":true} to every volumePrism item in data/practice-studio/5-10.json and make assets/studio-gen/geometry.js §5 honour it: L1 = unit cubes of 1/2 unit (count = 8 × volume; draw the half-unit grid), L2 = one edge a mixed number or a half (volume as a decimal or fraction), L3 = missing edge when another edge is fractional, L4 = two fractional edges and a comparison. Print figure labels in the same notation as the stem (7 1/2 on the figure when the stem says 7 1/2). Extend tools/studio-gen.test.mjs: for p.frac every draw has at least one non-integer edge and the independent check() recomputes the volume as a fraction.

widgets.component: sizer at level 2: edges move in whole-number steps
widgets.root: assets/studio-act/sizer.js uses step 1 at levels 1-2, so the one manipulable item in the Practice studio cannot produce a fractional edge. Only the Challenge sizers (L3 half steps, L4 quarter steps) do.
widgets.replacement: Give the item p:{"shape":"prism","goal":"volume","frac":true} and make make() use step 0.5 with targets that need one half-edge at level 2 (for example target 18 with l = 4, w = 3 → h = 1.5), keeping the readout 'l × w × h' with the student's numbers and the layer picture.

widgets.component: Connect check: 'What is the tank's volume?', 'About how many gallons does the tank hold?', 'Why divide by 231 instead of multiplying?' (now carried with the Connect scenario text and the Connect diagram)
widgets.root: The scenario text carries every number the three items need (checked against the answer keys: tank 24 × 12 × 16 in and 231 cubic inches per gallon), so the items are answerable. There is no figure, which is a missed chance to show the shape but not a defect.

widgets.where: Challenge §3.1-3.2 act:sizer L3, L4 (prism, goal volume), §3.3 (match)
widgets.component: sizer with half-unit and quarter-unit steps; match boxes with fractional edges to volumes
widgets.root: This is the model the lesson needs: sliders with 0.5 and 0.25 steps so the student must set edges like 2.5 or 1.75 and reads l × w × h with those values; match gives 6, 9, 2 and 10 ft³ from 3/4 × 4 × 2, 1 1/2 × 2 × 3, 1/2 × 1/2 × 8, 2 1/2 × 4 × 1.

widgets.component: detective items (rounded 1.5 down, 1 1/2 written as 11/2, cube volume 1/8 per half-inch cube), 'multiplying makes numbers bigger', boss items
widgets.root: Recomputed 18, 9, 2 in³, Max is right (12 in³), 10.5 ft³, 2.5 × 3 × 4, Box A = Box B = 15 in³, 6 ÷ 3 = 2 ft, 1.125 ÷ 1/4 = 4.5 → 5 bags. Fraction notation follows the stem (mixed numbers) throughout.

formulaOrder.formula: V = l × w × h = B × h with fractional edge lengths

typography: Challenge 5.1 and 2.4 figures print 3.5 ft, 1.5 ft and 1.5 cm while their stems write 3 1/2 ft, 1 1/2 ft and 1.5 cm; gen:volumePrism figures print 7.5 where the stem says 7 1/2.
